issue.name: Cross-site scripting (reflected)
issue.issueBackground: Reflected cross-site scripting vulnerabilities arise when data is copied from a request and echoed into the application's immediate response in an unsafe way.
issue.remediationBackground:
In most situations where user-controllable data is copied into application responses:

  • Input should be validated as strictly as possible.
  • User input should be HTML-encoded at any point where it is copied.
issue.vulnerabilityClassifications:
• CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
  • CWE-116: Improper Encoding
issue.issueDetail: The value of the q request parameter is copied into the HTML document as plain text between tags. The payload <script>alert(1)</script> was submitted.

issue.name: Cross-site scripting (reflected)
issue.issueBackground: Reflected cross-site scripting vulnerabilities arise when data is copied from a request and echoed into the application's immediate response in an unsafe way.
issue.remediationBackground: In most situations where user-controllable data is copied into application responses:
issue.issueDetail: The value of the filter request parameter is copied into a JavaScript string.

issue.name: Strict transport security not enforced
issue.issueBackground: The application fails to prevent users from connecting to it over unencrypted connections.

issue.name: Email addresses disclosed
issue.issueBackground: The presence of email addresses within application responses does not necessarily constitute a security vulnerability.
issue.issueDetail: The following email address was disclosed: sales@example.com
